च,
 I. A copulative particle, And. Where two things are to be joined, it is,
 1. Repeated, च--च (like τε--τε; Lat. que--que), As well--As, and, संजीवयति चाजस्रं प्रमापयति चाव्ययः, That immutable power revivifies as well as destroys in eternal succession,
; दश चाष्टौ च, Ten and eight,

. Dropped in the first place; this is the general use, Hit. i. d. 33.
 3. Dropped, but not often, in the second place, e. g. प्रेत्य चेह, In the next world and in this,

. Where more than two things are to be joined, some have the conjunction, while others are without it, e. g. कर्णौ चर्म च बालांश् च वस्तिं स्नायुं च रोचनाम्, (let him carry) their ears, their hides, their tails, the skin below their navels, their tendons, and the liquor exuding from their foreheads,

.
 II. When followed by वा, Either,

.
 III. Even, Śāk. 6, 5; and even, Hiḍ. i. 26. []
 IV. Just,

.
 V. But, Hit. Pr. d. 12.
 VI. If,

.
 --Cf. τε; Lat. que; Goth. -h, e. g. in sa-h, ‘and he.’
